current_direction_basis: Driven by 2025-2026 items collected here, not the older curiosity/Autism-Glass biography. (1) LLM mental-health safety: 'Characterizing Delusional Spirals through Human-LLM Chat Logs' (FAccT '26, Jun 2026) plus 'Expressing stigma and inappropriate responses prevents LLMs from safely replacing mental health providers' (FAccT 2025), reinforced by the Feb 6 2026 TechCrunch interview describing him as 'a Stanford professor researching the therapeutic potential of LLMs'. (2) User modeling: 'Learning Next Action Predictors from Human-Computer Interaction' (arXiv 2603.05923, Mar 6 2026) and the Stanford Screenomics platform papers (medRxiv 2025; JMIR Formative Research 2026). (3) 3D VLA models: '3D-GENERALIST' (3DV 2026) and 'LayoutVLM' (CVPR 2025). (4) RL for reasoning: 'Big-Math' and 'Just Enough Thinking: Efficient Reasoning with Adaptive Length Penalties Reinforcement Learning' and 'Towards System 2 Reasoning in LLMs' (all 2025). (5) AI in education: 'CogGen' (2025) and 'Scaffold or Crutch? Examining College Students' Use and Views of Generative AI Tools for STEM Education' (2025), alongside his 2025-26 course listings.

evidence.title: Learning Next Action Predictors from Human-Computer Interaction
evidence.summary: Preprint submitted 6 Mar 2026 formalizing 'next action prediction' (NAP): given a user's multimodal computer interactions (screenshots, clicks, sensor data), predict the next action. Labels 360K+ actions over one month of continuous phone usage from 20 users (1,800 hours of screen time) and introduces LongNAP, a user model trained via policy gradient methods that outperforms supervised finetuning and prompted baselines by 79% and 39%. Haber is a listed author alongside Omar Shaikh, Kanishk Gandhi, Michael S. Bernstein and Diyi Yang.

evidence.title: Characterizing Delusional Spirals through Human-LLM Chat Logs
evidence.summary: Conference paper at FAccT '26 (issued 2026-06-25) analyzing human-LLM chat logs for delusional spirals. Crossref author list confirms Nick Haber as an author (with Jared Moore, Kevin Klyman, Stevie Chancellor, Desmond C. Ong and others). Continues his line of work on LLM behavior in mental-health-adjacent conversation.

evidence.title: 3D-GENERALIST: Vision-Language-Action Models for Crafting 3D Worlds

evidence.title: The backlash over OpenAI's decision to retire GPT-4o shows how dangerous AI companions can be (TechCrunch)
evidence.summary: TechCrunch article dated February 6, 2026 quoting him at length. The piece describes 'Dr. Nick Haber, a Stanford professor researching the therapeutic potential of LLMs' and quotes him: 'I try to withhold judgment overall... I think we're getting into a very complex world around the sorts of relationships that people can have with these technologies' and 'We are social creatures, and there's certainly a challenge that these systems can be isolating.' It also states his 'own research has shown that chatbots respond inadequately when faced with various mental health conditions'. Linked from his Stanford GSE faculty page news section.

state_rationale: Very active researcher with strong 2026 evidence: three 2026 publications (arXiv Mar 2026, FAccT '26, 3DV 2026), six 2026-dated works in OpenAlex, and a February 6, 2026 TechCrunch interview. He is also listed on Stanford Profiles for CS 195 Supervised Undergraduate Research and CS 191 Senior Project in the current 2025-26 year, and the lab home page invites contact ('Interested in working with us? nhaber at stanford dot edu'). However, no explicit currently-open undergraduate position or program was found on any page fetched: the lab website has no join/openings page (404s), lists no undergraduate members, carries a '©2020' footer, and its publications page stops at 2022. The CS 195/CS 191 entries are standard catalog listings carried by many Stanford CS faculty, not a recruiting statement, so they do not meet the bar for OPENING. A cold email from a Stanford undergraduate is well-founded here -- the recent LLM-mental-health, next-action-prediction, and 3D-VLA lines are all live, and the contact-us line plus the CS 195/191 listings give a concrete mechanism to propose.
